newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice firms on contract covering, Iraq talks.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice firms on contract covering, Iraq talks.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to firmer this week as rising fresh supplies offset bullish demand, trade sources said on Thursday.
Traders said active post-holiday buying and talk of Iraq buying at least 30,000 tonnes of Thai rice bouyed the market.
Market sources said Iraq has bought 15 percent Thai white rice from recent tenders at about $355 per tonne FOB Bangkok.
"Besides that, there were no new major orders...only moderate amounts from our regular customers," said a trader.
"But there are many ships coming in for loading. That's why the demand is rising," he said.
Benchmark 100 white B was quoted at $335-360 per tonne FOB Bangkok against $325-355 last week. The 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted at $615-625 against $615-620 a week ago.
The market was also awaiting a Philippine rice production survey due later this month which, Thai traders hope, may lead to it buying rice from Thailand.

The Philippines is likely to import 150,000-200,000 tonnes of rice in the first quarter of 1997 but will wait for its output survey before placing any orders, according to a senior agriculture ministry official in Manila.
A senior Thai commerce ministry official said after a recent visit to Manila that the Philippines had expressed an interest in buying Thai rice.
Thailand aims to export at least five million tonnes of rice this year against an estimated 5.25 million in 1996.
